# Clients

Local clients start ameriflux-mcp themselves over **stdio**; hosted deployments are
reached over **Streamable HTTP**. The [install script](install.md#option-1-from-source-with-the-install-script-recommended)
(`scripts/install.sh`) writes the stdio entries below for Claude Code, Claude Desktop,
Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Goose and OpenCode in one step; this page shows them for manual
setup. The examples use `ameriflux-mcp` on your `PATH` (see [Install](install.md));
replace it with an absolute path such as
`/home/me/ameriflux-mcp/.venv/bin/ameriflux-mcp` (Windows:
`C:\\Users\\me\\ameriflux-mcp\\.venv\\Scripts\\ameriflux-mcp.exe`) when the client does
not share your shell's `PATH`. JSON-configured clients do not expand `~` or `$HOME`, so
use absolute paths there.

The examples register the server **without** a download identity, which is all that
discovery, variables, citations and local previews need. To enable downloads, add the
variables from [Download identity](identity.md#the-settings) to the same `env` block
(or `-e` options); keep them in the client's environment settings, never in a shared or
committed file.

## Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add ameriflux -s user -- ameriflux-mcp --transport stdio
claude mcp list
```

`-s user` makes the server available in every project[^claude-code-mcp]. Add
`-e NAME=value` options before `--` for the download identity.

## Claude Desktop

Edit `claude_desktop_config.json` and restart the app:

- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
- Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
- Linux: `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ameriflux": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/ameriflux-mcp",
      "args": ["--transport", "stdio"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Codex CLI

```bash
codex mcp add ameriflux -- ameriflux-mcp --transport stdio
codex mcp list
```

This writes the server into `~/.codex/config.toml`[^codex-mcp]; restart running
sessions. Without the CLI, add the table yourself:

```toml
[mcp_servers.ameriflux]
command = "/absolute/path/to/ameriflux-mcp"
args = []

# only for downloads:
# [mcp_servers.ameriflux.env]
# AMERIFLUX_USER_ID = "your-username"
```

## Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini mcp add --scope user ameriflux ameriflux-mcp
gemini mcp list
```

or add the entry to `~/.gemini/settings.json`[^gemini-mcp] (`.gemini/settings.json` in a
project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ameriflux": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/ameriflux-mcp",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}
```

## Goose

Add an extension to `~/.config/goose/config.yaml` (Windows:
`%APPDATA%\Block\goose\config\config.yaml`)[^goose-ext], then restart Goose Desktop or
start a new CLI session. `goose configure` → *Add Extension* → *Command-line Extension*
does the same interactively.

```yaml
extensions:
  ameriflux:
    enabled: true
    type: stdio
    name: ameriflux
    cmd: /absolute/path/to/ameriflux-mcp
    args: []
    envs: {}
    timeout: 300
```

## OpenCode

Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`[^opencode-mcp]. This is the layout OpenCode's
documentation shows. The install script writes `"mcp": {"servers": {…}}` instead unless
`opencode --version` reports 1.x; if your OpenCode does not pick the server up, move the
entry to the layout its documentation gives.

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "ameriflux": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["/absolute/path/to/ameriflux-mcp", "--transport", "stdio"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## VS Code

Add to `.vscode/mcp.json` in a workspace, or to your user configuration[^vscode-mcp].
For downloads, `inputs` prompts keep your identity out of the file:

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    { "type": "promptString", "id": "amf-user", "description": "AmeriFlux user ID" },
    { "type": "promptString", "id": "amf-email", "description": "Email registered with AmeriFlux", "password": true }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "ameriflux": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/ameriflux-mcp",
      "args": ["--transport", "stdio"],
      "env": {
        "AMERIFLUX_USER_ID": "${input:amf-user}",
        "AMERIFLUX_USER_EMAIL": "${input:amf-email}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Leave out `inputs` and `env` to run without downloads.

## Any other stdio client

Run `ameriflux-mcp --transport stdio` (bare `ameriflux-mcp` does the same), with the
download identity in the environment if you want downloads. The server speaks MCP
2026-07-28 and still accepts clients on earlier protocol revisions over stdio.

## A hosted server (HTTP)

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http ameriflux https://ameriflux-mcp.example.org/mcp
```

A hosted server offers the eight tools that need no identity and read no local files:
site search, site details, availability, the two variable tools, citations, BADM and
`amf_ping`. Downloads and the local file tools exist only on stdio, and no identity is
accepted over HTTP, by header or otherwise.

[^claude-code-mcp]: Claude Code — MCP. <https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp>
[^codex-mcp]: OpenAI Codex CLI. <https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/>
[^gemini-mcp]: Gemini CLI — MCP servers. <https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/tools/mcp-server.md>
[^goose-ext]: Goose — Using extensions. <https://goose-docs.ai/docs/getting-started/using-extensions>
[^opencode-mcp]: OpenCode — MCP servers. <https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/>
[^vscode-mcp]: VS Code — Use MCP servers. <https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers>

# Configuration

ameriflux-mcp runs with no configuration at all: the defaults serve stdio, cache
AmeriFlux API responses, keep tool results small, strip contact emails and confine
downloads to `~/ameriflux-downloads`. Settings come from four layers; a higher layer
wins:

1. **Command-line flags** (only a handful of common settings).
2. **Environment variables** named `AMERIFLUX_MCP_<SECTION>__<FIELD>`, with a double
   underscore descending into nested sections at any depth, for example
   `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__CATALOG=3600`. List settings take a comma-separated
   value: `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LOCAL__ROOTS=/data/fluxnet2015,/data/shared`. The empty string,
   `none` and `null` mean "unset".
3. **A YAML file** passed with `--config path.yaml`, using the same section and field
   names.
4. **Built-in defaults** (the table below).

Unknown keys in the YAML file or the environment are ignored with a warning, so a typo
does not stop the server but is visible in its log. Invalid values stop the server with
exit code 2 and a message naming the setting and the rule, never the value you gave (so a
mistyped email does not end up in a log). ameriflux-mcp does not load `.env` files
itself; export the variables (`set -a; . ./.env; set +a`) before starting it.

The table at the end is generated from the code[^config-module]
(`scripts/gen_config_reference.py`); CI fails if it drifts. Some settings configure
tools that arrive in later build steps (previews, downloads, the cache); they are
accepted now so configuration files do not need to change later.

## The download identity

Identity is read from the environment or the YAML file only, never from flags or tool
arguments, and is used only by the download tool. The plain names
(`AMERIFLUX_USER_ID`, `AMERIFLUX_USER_EMAIL`, `AMERIFLUX_USER_NAME`,
`AMERIFLUX_INTENDED_USE`, `AMERIFLUX_DESCRIPTION`) are what other AmeriFlux tools use;
the namespaced `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__…` forms take precedence when set.
`AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__IS_TEST` has no plain form and no default. Look-alike names
(`AMERIFLUX_EMAIL`, `AMERIFLUX_USERNAME`, `AMERIFLUX_USER`, `AMERIFLUX_TOKEN`,
`AMERIFLUX_API_KEY`, `AMF_USER_ID`, `AMF_USER_EMAIL`, `AMF_EMAIL`) are not read; the
server logs a warning, without the value, when one is set. See
[Download identity](identity.md) for what each value is and who sees it.

## Command-line flags

| Flag | Sets |
| --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | YAML file to load |
| `--transport {stdio,http}` | `server.transport` |
| `--bind-address`, `--bind-port` | `server.bind_address`, `server.bind_port` |
| `--log-level` | `server.log_level` |
| `--download-dir PATH` | `downloads.directory` |
| `--no-downloads` | `downloads.enabled = false` |
| `--print-config` | print the effective configuration as YAML (identity shown as `***`) and exit |
| `--check` | load the configuration, call `amf_ping` in-process (no network request), print a JSON report, exit 0 or 1 |
| `--version` | print the version |

## A YAML example

```yaml
# ameriflux-mcp.yaml — pass with: ameriflux-mcp --config ameriflux-mcp.yaml
identity:
  profiles:
    default:
      intended_use: other_research
      description: "Comparing drought responses of semi-arid grassland GPP across New Mexico towers."
downloads:
  directory: /data/ameriflux-downloads
local:
  roots: [/data/fluxnet2015]          # FLUXNET2015 zips you downloaded from fluxnet.org
cache:
  disk_dir: /data/cache/ameriflux-mcp
server:
  log_level: info
```

Keep the user ID and email in the environment rather than in a YAML file you share or
commit.

## Automatic values

* `downloads.enabled`: the download tool exists only on stdio; over HTTP it is never
  listed, whatever this says. `--no-downloads` (or `false`) removes it on stdio too.
* `cache.disk_dir`: the on-disk cache is on for stdio and off for HTTP unless a
  directory is configured, so containers without a writable home still start.
* `privacy.allow_contact_emails`: off on every transport. Contact emails of tower teams
  and DOI contributors appear only when this is on **and** a tool call asks for
  contacts.

## All settings

| Setting (YAML path) | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream.api_base_url` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__API_BASE_URL` | str | `https://amfcdn.lbl.gov/api` | AmeriFlux API base URL (v1 and v2 paths are appended per endpoint). |
| `upstream.user_agent_suffix` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__USER_AGENT_SUFFIX` | str \| null | unset | Text appended to the User-Agent header. |
| `upstream.connect_timeout_s` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S` | float | `10.0` | TCP/TLS connect timeout. |
| `upstream.read_timeout_s` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__READ_TIMEOUT_S` | float | `60.0` | Default read timeout. |
| `upstream.download_read_timeout_s` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__DOWNLOAD_READ_TIMEOUT_S` | float | `300.0` | Read timeout for data file downloads. |
| `upstream.requests_per_second` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__REQUESTS_PER_SECOND` | float | `2.0` | Rate limit towards the AmeriFlux API (local policy). |
| `upstream.max_concurrency` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__MAX_CONCURRENCY` | int | `4` | Maximum simultaneous upstream requests. |
| `upstream.max_response_bytes` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` | int | `20971520` | Largest upstream response body read into memory (the site catalog is 1.7 MB). |
| `upstream.retries.max_attempts` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__RETRIES__MAX_ATTEMPTS` | int | `3` | Attempts per upstream call, including the first. |
| `upstream.retries.backoff_base_s` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__RETRIES__BACKOFF_BASE_S` | float | `0.5` | Base of the exponential backoff (0.5 * 2^n seconds). |
| `upstream.retries.backoff_max_s` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__RETRIES__BACKOFF_MAX_S` | float | `8.0` | Cap on a single backoff sleep. |
| `upstream.retries.retry_after_default_s` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_UPSTREAM__RETRIES__RETRY_AFTER_DEFAULT_S` | float | `1.0` | Wait used on HTTP 429 when no Retry-After header is sent. |
| `identity.user_id` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__USER_ID`<br>(or `AMERIFLUX_USER_ID`) | SecretStr \| null | unset | AmeriFlux username sent with downloads (or AMERIFLUX_USER_ID). |
| `identity.user_email` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__USER_EMAIL`<br>(or `AMERIFLUX_USER_EMAIL`) | SecretStr \| null | unset | Email registered with AmeriFlux, sent with downloads (or AMERIFLUX_USER_EMAIL). |
| `identity.user_name` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__USER_NAME`<br>(or `AMERIFLUX_USER_NAME`) | SecretStr \| null | unset | Optional name sent with downloads (or AMERIFLUX_USER_NAME). |
| `identity.profiles.<name>.intended_use` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__PROFILES__<NAME>__INTENDED_USE`<br>(default profile: `AMERIFLUX_INTENDED_USE`) | `synthesis` \| `model` \| `remote_sensing` \| `other_research` \| `education` \| `other` \| null | unset | Intended-use category: 1-6 or synthesis, model, remote_sensing, other_research, education, other. |
| `identity.profiles.<name>.description` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__PROFILES__<NAME>__DESCRIPTION`<br>(default profile: `AMERIFLUX_DESCRIPTION`) | str \| null | unset | How you will use the data, in your own words (20-1000 characters); ' [ameriflux-mcp]' is appended when sent. |
| `identity.is_test` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__IS_TEST` | bool \| null | unset | Send downloads as test requests. Must be set before any download. |
| `cache.enabled` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__ENABLED` | bool | `true` | Cache AmeriFlux API responses. |
| `cache.max_entries` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__MAX_ENTRIES` | int | `1024` | Overall in-memory entry cap. |
| `cache.stale_if_error_s` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__STALE_IF_ERROR_S` | int | `604800` | How long an expired entry may be served when a refresh fails. |
| `cache.disk_dir` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__DISK_DIR` | Path \| null | unset | On-disk cache (personal fields removed). Unset: ~/.cache/ameriflux-mcp on stdio, none over http. |
| `cache.ttl_s.catalog` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__CATALOG` | int | `21600` | Site catalog (6 h). |
| `cache.ttl_s.availability` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__AVAILABILITY` | int | `21600` | Availability lists (6 h). |
| `cache.ttl_s.fluxnet2015` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__FLUXNET2015` | int | `2592000` | Frozen FLUXNET2015 and FLUXNET-CH4 lists (30 d). |
| `cache.ttl_s.variables` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__VARIABLES` | int | `86400` | FP Standard variable list (24 h). |
| `cache.ttl_s.citations` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__CITATIONS` | int | `86400` | DOI citations (24 h, memory only). |
| `cache.ttl_s.dictionaries` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__DICTIONARIES` | int | `2592000` | FLUXNET variable dictionaries (30 d). |
| `cache.ttl_s.heights` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__HEIGHTS` | int | `86400` | Measurement heights (24 h). |
| `cache.ttl_s.coverage` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__COVERAGE` | int | `604800` | Variable coverage snapshots (7 d). |
| `limits.default_limit` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__DEFAULT_LIMIT` | int | `25` | Default page size where a tool does not set its own. |
| `limits.max_limit` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__MAX_LIMIT` | int | `200` | Largest page size any tool accepts. |
| `limits.max_result_bytes` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__MAX_RESULT_BYTES` | int | `50000` | Tool results are trimmed (with page.truncated) to fit this many bytes of compact JSON. |
| `limits.hard_max_result_bytes` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__HARD_MAX_RESULT_BYTES` | int | `200000` | A result still larger than this after trimming fails with result_too_large. |
| `limits.max_resource_bytes` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__MAX_RESOURCE_BYTES` | int | `1048576` | Largest resource read returned; larger ones fail with result_too_large. |
| `limits.preview_max_rows` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__PREVIEW_MAX_ROWS` | int | `500` | Most rows amf_preview_data returns. |
| `limits.preview_scan_max_bytes` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__PREVIEW_SCAN_MAX_BYTES` | int | `268435456` | Most bytes a preview scans (256 MiB). |
| `limits.preview_time_budget_s` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__PREVIEW_TIME_BUDGET_S` | float | `20.0` | Wall-clock budget for one preview scan. |
| `limits.zip_member_max_bytes` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__ZIP_MEMBER_MAX_BYTES` | int | `1073741824` | Largest zip member read (uncompressed). |
| `limits.tools_list_max_bytes` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LIMITS__TOOLS_LIST_MAX_BYTES` | int | `80000` | Conformance bound on the serialized tools/list result (59,945 B with the 11 stdio tools of step 6; reset to measured x1.25 in step 8, as in neon-mcp). |
| `downloads.enabled` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_DOWNLOADS__ENABLED` | bool \| null | unset | Offer the download tool. Unset: true on stdio; never available over http. |
| `downloads.directory` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_DOWNLOADS__DIRECTORY` | Path | `~/ameriflux-downloads` | Directory every download is confined to (created on first use). |
| `downloads.max_files_per_call` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_DOWNLOADS__MAX_FILES_PER_CALL` | int | `50` | Most files one download call transfers. |
| `downloads.max_bytes_per_call` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_DOWNLOADS__MAX_BYTES_PER_CALL` | int | `2147483648` | Most bytes one download call transfers (2 GiB). |
| `downloads.max_file_bytes` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_DOWNLOADS__MAX_FILE_BYTES` | int | `1073741824` | Largest single file accepted (1 GiB). |
| `local.roots` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_LOCAL__ROOTS` | list[Path] | `[]` | Extra directories the local file tools may read (the download directory is always included), e.g. FLUXNET2015 zips from fluxnet.org. |
| `privacy.allow_contact_emails` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_PRIVACY__ALLOW_CONTACT_EMAILS` | bool | `false` | Allow team and contributor emails in results when a call asks for contacts. |
| `server.transport` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__TRANSPORT` | `stdio` \| `http` | `stdio` | stdio (local clients) or http (stateless Streamable HTTP at /mcp). |
| `server.bind_address` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__BIND_ADDRESS` | str | `127.0.0.1` | HTTP bind address. |
| `server.bind_port` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__BIND_PORT` | int | `8080` | HTTP bind port. |
| `server.public_base_url` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | str \| null | unset | Public URL of a hosted deployment; its host/origin join the allow-lists. |
| `server.allowed_hosts` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__ALLOWED_HOSTS` | list[str] | `[]` | Host header allow-list (DNS-rebinding protection). |
| `server.allowed_origins` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | list[str] | `[]` | Origin header allow-list (DNS-rebinding protection). |
| `server.dns_rebinding_protection` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__DNS_REBINDING_PROTECTION` | bool \| null | unset | Force DNS-rebinding protection on/off. Unset: SDK default (on for loopback binds or when allow-lists are set). |
| `server.json_response` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__JSON_RESPONSE` | bool | `false` | Answer POST /mcp with application/json instead of a single SSE frame. |
| `server.max_request_body_size` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE` | int | `1048576` | Largest accepted request body in bytes. |
| `server.tools_list_ttl_ms` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__TOOLS_LIST_TTL_MS` | int | `300000` | ttlMs advertised on tools/list. |
| `server.log_level` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__LOG_LEVEL` | `debug` \| `info` \| `warning` \| `error` \| `critical` | `info` | Log verbosity. |
| `server.instructions_extra` | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA` | str \| null | unset | Text appended to the server instructions. |

    resource: "https://amfcdn.lbl.gov/create"
    title: "FLUX User Account Creation (AmeriFlux and FLUXNET)"
    author: "team:ameriflux"
  - id: fluxnet-policy
    resource: "https://fluxnet.org/data/data-policy/"
    title: "FLUXNET Data Policy"
    author: "team:fluxnet"
  - id: research
    resource: "https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp/blob/main/RESEARCH.md"

# Download identity

Most of ameriflux-mcp needs no account at all: finding sites, checking which years
exist, describing variables, getting citations and previewing files you already have
all work anonymously. Only **downloading data from AmeriFlux** needs an identity, and
this page explains why, what is disclosed, and how to configure it.

!!! info "Available from build step 7"

    The download tool (`amf_download_data`) is the seventh build step, and it ships only
    once AmeriFlux confirms that third-party clients may use its download request. Until
    then you can store an identity with the installer, but nothing uses it.

## What a download discloses, and to whom

AmeriFlux has no API keys. Every download is a request that carries your AmeriFlux user
ID, your email, an intended-use category and a short description of how you will use
the data. AmeriFlux sends that information to the **principal investigators (PIs) of
each site** you download, and posts it to the AmeriFlux Data Download Log (visible to
logged-in users)[^amf-policy]. This is how tower teams learn who uses their data and
offer collaboration, so the text should be accurate and written by you.

ameriflux-mcp therefore follows four rules:

1. **Your words, not the model's.** The identity, intended use and description come only
   from configuration you wrote. They are never tool arguments, so an AI agent cannot
   invent or edit them. The server appends ` [ameriflux-mcp]` to the description so
   AmeriFlux can see which client sent the request.
2. **See it first.** A download request first returns a *plan*: the exact text that will
   be sent, the sites it goes to, and the data policy that applies. Nothing is sent.
3. **Then confirm.** Only a second call with `confirm=true`, naming the data policy you
   accept, sends the request.
4. **Only on your machine.** The download tool exists only over stdio, on the computer
   where your agent runs. A hosted (HTTP) ameriflux-mcp never accepts an identity.

ameriflux-mcp never builds download links itself and never uses unofficial mirrors: every
file comes through AmeriFlux's logged route, so PIs are notified as they are for
downloads from the AmeriFlux website.

## Create an AmeriFlux account

AmeriFlux and FLUXNET share one account system. Create an account on the
[FLUX User Account Creation](https://amfcdn.lbl.gov/create){target=_blank} page[^amf-account]:
full name, institution, email, and a **username**. The username is your AmeriFlux user
ID. The same page links to username lookup and password reset.

A registered account matters most for data under the **AmeriFlux Legacy** policy: the
AmeriFlux website offers Legacy data only to logged-in users. Whether AmeriFlux's API
checks the user ID against registered accounts has not been confirmed yet[^research] (question Q2
in the project's [support questions](https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp/blob/main/research/questions.md){target=_blank}).

## The settings

| Setting | Environment variable | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| User ID | `AMERIFLUX_USER_ID` | yes | Your AmeriFlux username. |
| Email | `AMERIFLUX_USER_EMAIL` | yes | The email registered with AmeriFlux. |
| Name | `AMERIFLUX_USER_NAME` | no | Shown to PIs alongside your email. |
| Intended use | `AMERIFLUX_INTENDED_USE` | yes | A code from the table below. |
| Description | `AMERIFLUX_DESCRIPTION` | yes | 20–1000 characters, in your own words. |
| Test requests | `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__IS_TEST` | yes | `true` or `false`; no default (see [below](#is_test)). |

Each also has a namespaced form (`AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__USER_ID`, …) that wins when
both are set, for giving ameriflux-mcp a different identity from other AmeriFlux tools
that read the plain names. Look-alike names such as `AMERIFLUX_EMAIL`,
`AMERIFLUX_USERNAME`, `AMF_USER_ID`, `AMERIFLUX_TOKEN` or `AMERIFLUX_API_KEY` are
**not** read; the server warns if one is set.

**Intended use.** The six categories AmeriFlux's download form offers:

| Code | Key | Category sent to AmeriFlux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `synthesis` | Research - Multi-site synthesis |
| 2 | `model` | Research - Land model/Earth system model |
| 3 | `remote_sensing` | Research - Remote sensing |
| 4 | `other_research` | Research - Other |
| 5 | `education` | Education (Teacher or Student) |
| 6 | `other` | Other |

**Profiles.** One description rarely fits every project. A YAML configuration file can
define named profiles, each with its own intended use and description, and a download
picks one with `profile="…"`; the environment variables above define the `default`
profile:

```yaml
# ameriflux-mcp.yaml — pass with: ameriflux-mcp --config ameriflux-mcp.yaml
identity:
  profiles:
    default:
      intended_use: other_research
      description: "Comparing drought responses of semi-arid grassland GPP across New Mexico towers."
    teaching:
      intended_use: education
      description: "Classroom exercises on energy-balance closure for an ecosystem ecology course."
```

Keep the user ID and email in the environment rather than in a file you might share.

### is_test

AmeriFlux's download request has an `is_test` flag. The AmeriFlux website sends `false`
for real downloads; other clients behave differently, and exactly what AmeriFlux does
with test requests (whether they are logged or sent to PIs) is not documented yet.
ameriflux-mcp therefore gives it **no default**: until you set
`AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__IS_TEST` to `true` (trying things out) or `false` (real
downloads for your work), the download tool refuses with `auth_required` and
`reason: is_test_unset`.

## Give it to ameriflux-mcp

=== "Install script"

    ```bash
    scripts/install.sh --with-identity
    ```

    The script reads the variables from your environment or asks for each missing one,
    validates them, and stores them in every agent's server `env`, with owner-only file
    permissions. See [Install](install.md#the-download-identity-and-the-script).

=== "Claude Code"

    ```bash
    claude mcp add ameriflux -s user \
      -e AMERIFLUX_USER_ID=your-username \
      -e AMERIFLUX_USER_EMAIL=you@example.edu \
      -e AMERIFLUX_INTENDED_USE=4 \
      -e AMERIFLUX_DESCRIPTION="Comparing drought responses of semi-arid grassland GPP." \
      -e AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__IS_TEST=false \
      -- ameriflux-mcp
    ```

=== "JSON clients"

    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "ameriflux": {
          "command": "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/ameriflux-mcp",
          "args": [],
          "env": {
            "AMERIFLUX_USER_ID": "your-username",
            "AMERIFLUX_USER_EMAIL": "you@example.edu",
            "AMERIFLUX_INTENDED_USE": "4",
            "AMERIFLUX_DESCRIPTION": "Comparing drought responses of semi-arid grassland GPP.",
            "AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__IS_TEST": "false"
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

Check it with `ameriflux-mcp --check` or by asking your agent to call `amf_ping`: the
result says which fields are configured, as booleans and profile names, never the values.

## Data policy at download time

Every AmeriFlux site shares its data under the **CC-BY-4.0** license or the more
restrictive **AmeriFlux Legacy** policy, and combining the two means following Legacy
for everything[^amf-policy]. FLUXNET2015 uses Tier 1 (CC-BY-4.0) and Tier 2[^fluxnet-policy].
The download plan states the policy that applies to the sites you chose, and
`confirm=true` must name it (`accept_data_policy="CCBY4.0"` or `"LEGACY"`), so you
accept the right terms. The AmeriFlux FLUXNET product exists only for CC-BY sites.
[Citing AmeriFlux and FLUXNET data](../about/citing-ameriflux.md) lists what each
policy asks of you.

## FLUXNET2015

FLUXNET2015 files are downloaded through a login-protected form on fluxnet.org that
also asks for an intended-use statement. ameriflux-mcp does not automate that form.
Download the zips yourself, put them in your download directory or a folder listed in
`local.roots` ([Configuration](configuration.md)), and the local file tools read them.

## Privacy

Your identity values are masked in logs, `--print-config` output and the installer's
output, and never written to caches, download records or test fixtures. ameriflux-mcp
also strips the contact emails of tower teams and DOI contributors from its results
unless you explicitly ask for contacts **and** the operator enabled
`privacy.allow_contact_emails` (off by default), for example to contact PIs as the
Legacy policy asks.

[^amf-policy]: AmeriFlux Data Policy. <https://ameriflux.lbl.gov/data/data-policy/>
[^amf-account]: FLUX User Account Creation. <https://amfcdn.lbl.gov/create>
[^fluxnet-policy]: FLUXNET Data Policy. <https://fluxnet.org/data/data-policy/>
[^research]: ameriflux-mcp verified research. <https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp/blob/main/RESEARCH.md>

# Install ameriflux-mcp

ameriflux-mcp is a Python 3.11+ package with one command, `ameriflux-mcp`, that MCP
clients start over stdio. These instructions cover macOS, Linux and Windows.

!!! warning "Under construction: build step 6 of 8"

    ameriflux-mcp is being built in eight steps (see the [roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md)).
    The server installs and starts on every client below, and site search, site details,
    data availability, variables, citations, BADM and local file previews work today;
    downloads arrive in step 7. The [tool reference](../tools/reference.md) always lists what the
    current build offers. Every step on this page works as written today.

!!! note "Private repository and no PyPI release yet"

    The repository is private for now, so you need read access to
    [idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp](https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp){target=_blank}[^repo]
    and git credentials (see [Access the repository](#access-the-repository)). The first
    PyPI release, as `ameriflux-mcp`, is the last build step.

## Prerequisites

- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/){target=_blank}[^uv], which installs Python 3.11+ for
  ameriflux-mcp if your system lacks it and keeps the server in its own environment.
- git, to clone the repository.
- Access to the private repository on GitHub, for example through the
  [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/){target=_blank}[^gh].
- Optional: an [AmeriFlux account](identity.md), only for downloading data. Everything
  else works without one.

### Install uv

=== "macOS"

    ```bash
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    # or: brew install uv
    ```

=== "Linux"

    ```bash
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    # or your distribution's package, if it ships uv 0.5 or newer
    ```

=== "Windows (PowerShell)"

    ```powershell
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
    # or: winget install --id=astral-sh.uv -e
    ```

Open a new terminal afterwards so `uv` is on your `PATH`, and check with
`uv --version`[^uv-install].

### Install git

=== "macOS"

    ```bash
    xcode-select --install        # Apple's command-line tools include git
    # or: brew install git
    ```

=== "Linux"

    ```bash
    sudo apt install git          # Debian, Ubuntu
    sudo dnf install git          # Fedora, RHEL
    ```

=== "Windows"

    ```powershell
    winget install --id Git.Git -e
    ```

    Git for Windows includes **Git Bash**, which the install script needs on Windows.

### Access the repository

While the repository is private, clone it with credentials GitHub accepts. The GitHub
CLI is the simplest route on every platform:

=== "macOS"

    ```bash
    brew install gh
    gh auth login                 # choose GitHub.com, HTTPS, and log in with a browser
    ```

=== "Linux"

    ```bash
    # install gh from https://cli.github.com/ (packages for apt, dnf, zypper, ...)
    gh auth login
    ```

=== "Windows (PowerShell)"

    ```powershell
    winget install --id GitHub.cli -e
    gh auth login
    ```

`gh auth login` also sets up git's credential helper, so plain `git clone https://…`
and `uv tool install git+https://…` work afterwards. An SSH key added to your GitHub
account works too: clone `git@github.com:idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp.git` instead.

## Option 1: From source with the install script (recommended)

=== "macOS / Linux"

    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp.git
    cd ameriflux-mcp
    scripts/install.sh
    ```

=== "Windows (Git Bash)"

    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp.git
    cd ameriflux-mcp
    scripts/install.sh --dry-run    # check the paths it will write first
    scripts/install.sh
    ```

`scripts/install.sh` creates the server environment (`uv sync`) if
`.venv/bin/ameriflux-mcp` is missing, checks that `ameriflux-mcp --version` runs, then
registers that executable with every supported agent it finds on your machine: Claude
Code, Claude Desktop, OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Goose and OpenCode. It prefers each
agent's own CLI when one is installed (`claude mcp add`, `codex mcp add`,
`gemini mcp add`) and otherwise merges an entry into the agent's config file, keeping
everything else in the file and leaving a `.bak` copy.

```bash
scripts/install.sh --with-identity               # also store your download identity (see below)
scripts/install.sh --agents all --dry-run        # preview the change for every agent
scripts/install.sh --agents claude,goose         # just Claude Code and Goose
scripts/install.sh --scope project               # project-level config (claude, codex, gemini, opencode)
scripts/install.sh --env AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__LOG_LEVEL=debug   # any extra environment variable
scripts/install.sh --command "$(command -v ameriflux-mcp)"       # register a uv-tool install instead
scripts/install.sh --uninstall                   # remove the registration everywhere
```

| Agent | What the script does |
| --- | --- |
| `claude` (Claude Code) | `claude mcp add --scope user ameriflux -- /path/to/ameriflux-mcp/.venv/bin/ameriflux-mcp` |
| `claude-desktop` | adds `mcpServers.ameriflux` to `claude_desktop_config.json` |
| `codex` (OpenAI Codex CLI) | `codex mcp add ameriflux -- …`, or an `[mcp_servers.ameriflux]` table in `~/.codex/config.toml` |
| `gemini` (Gemini CLI) | `gemini mcp add --scope user ameriflux …`, or `mcpServers.ameriflux` in `~/.gemini/settings.json` |
| `goose` | adds an `ameriflux` stdio extension to `~/.config/goose/config.yaml` |
| `opencode` | adds `mcp.servers.ameriflux` (v2) or `mcp.ameriflux` (v1) to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` |

The script writes the absolute path of the executable, because desktop apps do not
inherit your shell `PATH`. It needs bash; macOS's built-in bash 3.2 is enough. Restart
desktop apps (Claude Desktop, Goose Desktop) after installing.

### The download identity and the script

Only the download tool needs an identity, and everything in it is sent to the site
PIs when you confirm a download ([Download identity](identity.md) explains why). There
is deliberately no option that takes these values on the command line, since command
lines end up in shell history and process lists. `--with-identity` reads them from your
environment, or asks for each missing one on a terminal:

```bash
scripts/install.sh --with-identity
# AmeriFlux user ID: ...
# Email registered with AmeriFlux: ...
# Your name (optional, Enter to skip):
# Intended use (1 synthesis, 2 model, 3 remote sensing, 4 other research, 5 education, 6 other): ...
# Describe how you will use the data (20-1000 characters, in your own words): ...
# Send downloads as test requests? (true/false): ...
```

The answers are stored in each agent's server `env` as `AMERIFLUX_USER_ID`,
`AMERIFLUX_USER_EMAIL`, `AMERIFLUX_USER_NAME`, `AMERIFLUX_INTENDED_USE`,
`AMERIFLUX_DESCRIPTION` and `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__IS_TEST`.

- They are stored **in plain text** in each agent's config file. The script restricts
  the files it writes, and their `.bak` copies, to your user (mode `600`), and masks your
  user ID, email and name as `***` in everything it prints, including the output of the
  agent CLIs it calls.
- For agents registered through their own CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), the
  values are passed to that CLI's `mcp add` command and are briefly visible in the
  process list. Add `--prefer-files` to have Codex and Gemini CLI configured by file.
- Without `--with-identity` nothing is stored. Discovery, availability, variables,
  citations and local previews work as usual; the download tool explains what is
  missing when you ask it to download.

### Windows

On Windows, run the script from **Git Bash** (installed with Git for Windows) or
register by hand (Option 2). Git Bash converts paths to Windows form, uses
`.venv\Scripts\ameriflux-mcp.exe`, and writes Claude Desktop's config under
`%APPDATA%\Claude` and Goose's under `%APPDATA%\Block\goose\config`. Git Bash support
has not been tested as widely as macOS and Linux; check the result with `--dry-run`
first. Do not run the script inside WSL to configure Windows apps: it would write WSL's
own config files, which Claude Desktop for Windows never reads. (Inside WSL, for agents
that also run inside WSL, it works as on Linux.)

## Option 2: Install the package and register it by hand

=== "uv tool (recommended)"

    ```bash
    uv tool install git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp
    ```

    This puts `ameriflux-mcp` in uv's tool directory (`~/.local/bin` on macOS and
    Linux, `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` on Windows) and uses your git credentials for the
    private repository. Upgrade with
    `uv tool install --reinstall git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp`.

=== "From source"

    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp.git
    cd ameriflux-mcp
    uv sync                      # creates .venv with the package
    uv run ameriflux-mcp --version
    ```

=== "PyPI (from v0.1.0)"

    ```bash
    uv tool install ameriflux-mcp
    # or: pipx install ameriflux-mcp
    ```

    Not published yet; the PyPI release is build step 8.

Then find the executable's absolute path, which is what desktop apps need:

=== "macOS / Linux"

    ```bash
    command -v ameriflux-mcp     # e.g. /Users/you/.local/bin/ameriflux-mcp
    # from source: /path/to/ameriflux-mcp/.venv/bin/ameriflux-mcp
    ```

=== "Windows (PowerShell)"

    ```powershell
    (Get-Command ameriflux-mcp).Source  # e.g. C:\Users\you\.local\bin\ameriflux-mcp.exe
    # from source: C:\path\to\ameriflux-mcp\.venv\Scripts\ameriflux-mcp.exe
    ```

and register it with your client. The shortest form, for Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add ameriflux -s user -- ameriflux-mcp
```

Claude Desktop, and other JSON-configured clients:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ameriflux": {
      "command": "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/ameriflux-mcp",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}
```

Use absolute paths (not `~/` or `./`). On Windows escape backslashes:
`"C:\\Users\\You\\.local\\bin\\ameriflux-mcp.exe"`. To enable downloads, add an `env`
block with your identity ([Download identity](identity.md#give-it-to-ameriflux-mcp)).
[Clients](clients.md) has the entries for Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Goose,
OpenCode, VS Code and hosted servers.

## Option 3: Docker (from build step 8)

The repository will ship a `Dockerfile` that serves stateless Streamable HTTP on port
8080 as a non-root user, with a `/healthz` health check:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp.git && cd ameriflux-mcp
docker build -t ameriflux-mcp .
docker run --rm --read-only --tmpfs /tmp -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 ameriflux-mcp
```

Point an HTTP-capable client at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp`. Over HTTP the server
offers the eight discovery, variable and citation tools; downloads and local file tools
are stdio only, and no identity is ever accepted over HTTP.

## Verify the installation

```bash
ameriflux-mcp --version     # ameriflux-mcp 0.1.0
ameriflux-mcp --check       # {"ok": true, "version": "0.1.0", "protocolVersion": "2026-07-28", "transport": "stdio", "identityConfigured": false, "downloadsEnabled": true}
```

`--check` loads your configuration, calls `amf_ping` in-process and prints a one-line
JSON report: version, protocol, transport, whether a download identity is configured
(as booleans, never the values) and whether downloads are enabled. It makes no network
request. To check that AmeriFlux answers, ask your agent to call `amf_ping` with
`check_api=true` once the server is connected. `--print-config` shows the effective
settings with identity values replaced by `***`.

In Claude Code, `claude mcp list` runs a health check and shows `ameriflux` as
connected. To talk to the server directly over stdio:

```bash
# 2026-07-28 client: every request carries the protocol envelope in _meta
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"server/discover","params":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion":"2026-07-28","io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities":{},"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo":{"name":"manual","version":"0"}}}}' \
  | ameriflux-mcp

# 2025-era client: classic initialize handshake, then tools/list
printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"manual","version":"0"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
  | ameriflux-mcp
```

Both print JSON-RPC responses on stdout (logs go to stderr) and exit once stdin closes.
`server/discover` reports the server's capabilities and instructions; `tools/list` lists
every tool available in that build.

## Configuration

Nothing is required. The settings most people touch:

```bash
AMERIFLUX_MCP_SERVER__LOG_LEVEL=info           # debug | info | warning | error | critical (stderr)
AMERIFLUX_MCP_DOWNLOADS__DIRECTORY=            # where downloads go (default ~/ameriflux-downloads)
AMERIFLUX_MCP_LOCAL__ROOTS=                    # extra folders the file tools may read (e.g. FLUXNET2015 zips)
AMERIFLUX_MCP_DOWNLOADS__ENABLED=false         # turn the download tool off entirely
```

ameriflux-mcp does not read `.env` files on its own. See [Configuration](configuration.md)
for every setting, the YAML file and the precedence rules.

## Troubleshooting

**The install script says "nothing was registered".** `ameriflux-mcp --version` did not
run, so the script refused to register a broken command. Run `uv sync` in the clone (or
reinstall with `uv tool install --reinstall …`) and try again; run the command yourself
to see its error; `scripts/install.sh --dry-run` shows what it would do without stopping.

**The server exits at once with "invalid configuration".** A setting failed validation
(exit code 2). The message names the setting and the rule, for example
`identity.user_email: Value error, user_email is not an email address`; it never repeats
the value, so check the variable yourself. `ameriflux-mcp --print-config` shows the
effective settings once they load.

**`git clone` fails with "Repository not found" or asks for a password.** The repository
is private: GitHub answers 404 to anyone without access. Ask an idss-mesa maintainer for
access, then run `gh auth login` (or use SSH) so git sends your credentials.

**`ameriflux-mcp: command not found` from a desktop app.** Desktop apps do not read your
shell profile. Use the executable's absolute path as the `command`; the install script
does this for you.

**Server shows as disconnected.** Run the configured command yourself with `--check`. If
it fails, re-create the environment (`uv sync` in a clone, or
`uv tool install --reinstall git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp`). Claude
Desktop logs live in `~/Library/Logs/Claude/` (macOS) or `%APPDATA%\Claude\logs\`
(Windows); in Claude Code, `claude mcp get ameriflux` shows the connection status.

**`identityConfigured` is `false` although you set the variables.** They did not reach
the server process: desktop apps do not see variables exported in your shell. Put them in
the client's `env` block, or re-run the install script with `--with-identity`.

**Downloads report `auth_required` with `is_test_unset`.** `is_test` has no default on
purpose; set `AMERIFLUX_MCP_IDENTITY__IS_TEST` to `true` or `false` (see
[Download identity](identity.md#is_test)).

**Port already in use.** MCP over stdio uses no network port; a port error comes from an
HTTP deployment (`--transport http`, port 8080 by default) or something else on your
machine.

**Windows paths.** In JSON, write backslashes doubled (`C:\\Users\\…`) or use forward
slashes. Point at `ameriflux-mcp.exe`, not the extension-less name.

## Upgrading

```bash
# install script / from source
git pull origin main && uv sync
# uv tool
uv tool install --reinstall git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp
```

Registrations made by the install script keep pointing at `.venv/bin/ameriflux-mcp`, so
`git pull && uv sync` is enough; restart desktop apps afterwards.

## Uninstallation

`--uninstall` leaves each edited file's `.bak` copy behind; if you used
`--with-identity`, those backups (owner-only, like the files) still contain your user
ID and email, so delete them too.

```bash
scripts/install.sh --uninstall       # remove the server from every agent config
cd .. && rm -rf ameriflux-mcp        # if installed from source
uv tool uninstall ameriflux-mcp      # if installed with uv tool
rm -rf ~/.cache/ameriflux-mcp        # the response cache (from build step 3)
```

Downloaded data in `~/ameriflux-downloads` is yours; remove it separately if you no
longer need it.

- [Quickstart](quickstart.md): a first session.
- [Download identity](identity.md): what downloads disclose and how to configure them.
- [Clients](clients.md): per-client configuration.
- [Configuration](configuration.md): every setting.

[^uv]: uv documentation. <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/>
[^uv-install]: Installing uv. <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/>
[^gh]: GitHub CLI. <https://cli.github.com/>

# Quickstart

This walks through a first session in Claude Code[^claude-code-mcp]; other clients work
the same way once connected ([Clients](clients.md)).

!!! warning "A preview of the planned session"

    The tools below arrive in build steps 2–7 ([roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md)); the
    arguments and results follow the design[^design] and may change in detail before
    v0.1.0. Steps 2–5 and 7 below (`amf_ping`, site search, availability, variables,
    citations) work today; in step 6 the preview works on files you already have, and
    the download tool arrives in build step 7.

## 1. Register the server

```bash
claude mcp add ameriflux -s user -- ameriflux-mcp --transport stdio
```

No account is needed for this walkthrough. Downloads (step 6 below) need a
[download identity](identity.md).

## 2. Check it

Ask the agent to "call amf_ping with check_api=true". The result shows the version,
protocol `2026-07-28`, the transport, which download-identity fields are configured (as
booleans), whether downloads are enabled, and under `upstream` whether one small request
to the AmeriFlux API succeeded.

## 3. Find towers

```json
{"tool": "amf_search_sites", "arguments": {"igbp": ["DBF"], "state": ["MA"], "product": "FLUXNET", "min_years": 10}}
```

→ deciduous broadleaf forest sites in Massachusetts with at least ten years of
AmeriFlux FLUXNET data, each with `siteId` (such as `US-Ha1`, Harvard Forest), name,
location, IGBP class, data policy and the years per product. Sites also resolve by name
or NEON code: `amf_get_site(site="SRER")` finds `US-xSR`, the NEON Santa Rita tower, and
points to the matching NEON data product.

## 4. Check what data exist

```json
{"tool": "amf_get_availability", "arguments": {"sites": ["US-Ha1", "CA-Let"], "products": ["BASE-BADM", "FLUXNET"]}}
```

→ the published years per site and product[^amf-products]. `CA-Let` shares its data
under the Legacy policy, so it has BASE years but appears in `emptySites` for FLUXNET,
with a note that the FLUXNET product exists only for CC-BY sites.

## 5. Understand the variables

```json
{"tool": "amf_describe_variables", "arguments": {"names": ["GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "TA_F_MDS_QC"], "resolution": "DD"}}
```

→ `GPP_NT_VUT_REF` is gross primary production from nighttime partitioning with a
variable USTAR threshold, reference realization, in gC m-2 d-1 at daily resolution;
`TA_F_MDS_QC` is the fraction (0–1) of measured or good-quality gap-filled air
temperature in each day.

## 6. Plan a download

```json
{"tool": "amf_download_data", "arguments": {"sites": ["US-Ha1"], "product": "FLUXNET"}}
```

→ a **plan**, not a download: the exact user ID (masked), email (masked), intended use
and description that would be sent to the US-Ha1 PIs, the data policy (`CCBY4.0`) and
what it asks of you. Only `confirm=true` with `accept_data_policy="CCBY4.0"` sends the
request; the files land in `~/ameriflux-downloads` with a checksum record. Then
`amf_preview_data(site="US-Ha1", product="FLUXNET", resolution="DD")` summarizes the
daily file without loading it all.

## 7. Cite it

```json
{"tool": "amf_get_citation", "arguments": {"sites": ["US-Ha1"], "product": "FLUXNET"}}
```

→ the versioned citation AmeriFlux recommends ("… AmeriFlux FLUXNET-1F US-Ha1 Harvard
Forest EMS Tower (HFR1), Ver. v1.3_r1 (1991-2025), AmeriFlux AMP, (Dataset).
https://doi.org/10.17190/AMF/1871137"), the required acknowledgments, the processing
reference and a data-availability sentence. See
[Citing AmeriFlux and FLUXNET data](../about/citing-ameriflux.md).

Every result also carries `notes` (caveats) and `nextSteps` (concrete follow-up calls),
so agents normally chain these on their own.

[^claude-code-mcp]: Claude Code — MCP. <https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp>
[^amf-products]: AmeriFlux flux data products. <https://ameriflux.lbl.gov/data/flux-data-products/>
[^design]: ameriflux-mcp design. <https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp/blob/main/DESIGN.md>

# Citations and BADM

`amf_get_citation` gathers everything you need to credit a set of sites, and
`amf_get_badm` returns the site metadata the API exposes. Both work over stdio and HTTP
without an account. [Citing AmeriFlux and FLUXNET data](../about/citing-ameriflux.md)
explains the policies behind them.

## amf_get_citation

Give up to 50 sites and one product:

| `product` | Citation |
| --- | --- |
| `BASE-BADM` (default) | AmeriFlux's own text for the site's BASE DOI, with the version (`Ver. 28-5`) |
| `BIF` (BADM) | The BASE-BADM citation: BADM has no DOI of its own |
| `FLUXNET` (FLUXNET-1F) | AmeriFlux's text for the FLUXNET DOI (`Ver. v1.3_r1 (1991-2025)`) |
| `FLUXNET2015` | Built from the DOI record the way the FLUXNET DOI page shows it: authors, Tier Two years, title, "Dataset", DOI |

FLUXNET-CH4 citations come in v0.2 (`feature_unavailable` until then).

The result has:

- **`citations`**: one per site, cited as written in the reference list (not in
  supplementary material). `source` says where the text came from: `amfcdn` (AmeriFlux),
  `constructed` (FLUXNET2015) or `datacite` (a fallback when the AmeriFlux DOI service is
  down; it has no version and comes with a `versionMissing` warning). Set
  `include_bibtex` for a BibTeX entry per site.
- **`missing`**: requested sites without a citation and why (a Legacy site has no FLUXNET
  product; US-xSR is not part of FLUXNET2015).
- **`effectivePolicy`**: the policy the whole selection must follow, with each obligation
  marked `required` or `recommended`[^design]. Mixing CC-BY and Legacy sites means Legacy;
  any Tier Two site makes FLUXNET2015 Tier Two.
- **`acknowledgments`**: verbatim text from the policy page[^amf-policy]. Legacy data name
  the data *portal*, CC-BY data the data *service*, and FLUXNET adds the networks and ERA5
  text.
- **`siteFunding`**: under Legacy, each site's sponsors from its DOI record, to
  acknowledge. When a record has none, a note points to the site's BADM.
- **`dataAvailability`**: the sentence for a Data Availability section, with the product
  filled in and the AmeriFlux-listed `[SOURCE]` options.
- **`processingReferences`**: Chu et al. 2023 (BASE) or Pastorello et al. 2020 (FLUXNET,
  FLUXNET2015).

```json
{"tool": "amf_get_citation", "arguments": {"sites": ["US-Ha1", "CA-Let"]}}
{"tool": "amf_get_citation", "arguments": {"sites": ["US-Ha1", "RU-Sam"], "product": "FLUXNET2015"}}
```

The first call returns the Legacy policy, because CA-Let shares its data under it; the
second returns Tier Two, because RU-Sam is Tier Two only[^research].

## amf_get_badm

BADM (Biological, Ancillary, Disturbance and Metadata) for one site, grouped as the API
exposes it:

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `site` | Location (GRP_LOCATION), IGBP and climate with AmeriFlux's descriptions, tower dates, site URL, description |
| `team` | Names, roles and institutions; emails only under the two-flag rule ([Configuration](../getting-started/configuration.md)) |
| `disturbance` | Dominant disturbance and management, and the flux gas species measured |
| `funding` | Sponsor and contributor organizations from the DOI record: what a Legacy site asks you to acknowledge |
| `references` | The site's reference papers, paged (`references_limit`, `references_offset`) |
| `instruments` | Variables with height (m; negative is depth), instrument models and dates, from the measurement-height file; `variables` narrows them by base name (`TA`) or exact column (`SWC_1_1_1`) |

The complete BADM, with every group and its dates, is the BIF file inside each BASE-BADM
download.

```json
{"tool": "amf_get_badm", "arguments": {"site": "US-Ha1", "include": ["funding", "instruments"], "variables": ["TA"]}}
```

## Resources

| URI | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `ameriflux://guide/data-policy` | CC-BY-4.0 and Legacy, Tier One and Tier Two, and why mixing escalates |
| `ameriflux://reference/acknowledgments` | The verbatim texts, with the date they were checked against the policy pages[^fluxnet-policy] |

[^fluxnet-policy]: FLUXNET Data Policy. <https://fluxnet.org/data/data-policy/>

# Discovery and availability

Three tools answer "which towers, and what data do they have?" They read the AmeriFlux
site catalog and availability lists, which need no account, and work over stdio and
HTTP alike. Inputs and result fields are in the [Tool reference](reference.md).

## One catalog for three collections

ameriflux-mcp merges three lists into one catalog[^research], the same data the
[AmeriFlux site search](https://ameriflux.lbl.gov/sites/site-search/){target=_blank}[^amf-sites]
shows:

| Collection | Sites | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ameriflux` | about 856 | AmeriFlux sites across the Americas, with BASE and FLUXNET (FLUXNET-1F) years, data policy, DOIs, team, networks and measured variables |
| `fluxnet2015` | 212 | The frozen FLUXNET2015 release, worldwide, with Tier One (CC-BY-4.0) and Tier Two year ranges |
| `fluxnet_ch4` | 81 | The FLUXNET-CH4 Community Product V1.0 |

A tower in several lists is one site (US-Ha1 is in `ameriflux` and `fluxnet2015`). Sites
only in a FLUXNET list, such as DE-Tha, carry the sparser FLUXNET fields. The catalog is
cached for six hours, and on stdio also on disk, so a restarted server does not reload
it[^design].

## Naming a site

Every `site` or `sites` argument accepts:

- a site ID in any case: `US-Ha1`, `us-ha1`;
- a NEON site code: `SRER` is `US-xSR`;
- a FLUXNET2015 ID renamed after the release: `DK-ZaF` is `GL-ZaF` (with a note);
- a site name: `Santa Rita`, `Mayberry Wetland`.

Each interpretation is echoed in `resolved`. A name that fits several sites fails with
`ambiguous_input` and lists them (`Harvard Forest` gives US-Ha1, US-Ha2, US-Ha3, …): pick
one and call again.

## amf_search_sites

Filters combine (every filter must hold): words in the ID, name, place, NEON code or
networks (prefixes count: `harv`); `collection`; `product` and `policy`; IGBP class;
Köppen climate (prefixes: `B` is every dry climate); country (code as in site IDs, or
name); state or province; tower status; member network (`NEON`, `LTER`, `Phenocam`, …);
a bounding box or `near` a point; data years overlapping a window, or at least
`min_years`; measured BASE variables (`FCH4`); flux gas species (`CH4`).

Each site comes with its years per product, its policy and its member networks;
`facets` count every match by collection, IGBP, country, policy and status, so you can
see the shape of a large result before paging through it.

```json
{"tool": "amf_search_sites", "arguments": {"network": ["NEON"], "igbp": ["GRA"]}}
{"tool": "amf_search_sites", "arguments": {"near": {"latitude": 34.36, "longitude": -106.7, "radius_km": 60}}}
{"tool": "amf_search_sites", "arguments": {"collection": "fluxnet2015", "policy": "TIER2"}}
```

## amf_get_site

One site, with the ecosystem and climate described in AmeriFlux's own words (from the
[vocabularies](#resources)), the policy and what it asks of you, DOIs, years per
product, team (names, roles, institutions), measured BASE variables and links to other
networks:

- **NEON**: for NEON towers, the NEON site code and NEON's own flux product,
  DP4.00200.001, with a next step for the NEON MCP server.
- **LTER**: for sites in the [LTER crosswalk](#resources), the LTER site and its EDI
  scope, with a next step for the EDI MCP server. The crosswalk is curated and marked
  draft; each link says whether it comes from the upstream LTER tag or the site name.

Team emails are withheld unless you ask for contacts **and** the server's operator
enabled `privacy.allow_contact_emails` ([Configuration](../getting-started/configuration.md)).

!!! note "AmeriFlux's Köppen wording"

    AmeriFlux describes `Bsh` as "Steppe: very cold winter" and `Bsk` as "Steppe: warm
    winter", the reverse of standard Köppen-Geiger (BSh hot, BSk cold semi-arid). The
    text is passed on as AmeriFlux shows it, with a `koeppenNote` flagging the swap.

## amf_get_availability

The years each site has per product, from AmeriFlux's availability lists:

| Product | Policies | Rows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BASE-BADM` | CCBY4.0, LEGACY | years |
| `FLUXNET` (FLUXNET-1F) | CCBY4.0 only | years |
| `FLUXNET2015` | CCBY4.0, TIER2 | years |
| `FLUXNET-CH4` | CCBY4.0, TIER2 | years |
| `BIF` (BADM) | CCBY4.0, LEGACY | membership only: AmeriFlux publishes no BADM years |

Without a `policy`, every row is labelled with the policy its data are actually shared
under. LEGACY and TIER2 lists are supersets of the CC-BY lists (a CC-BY site may also
be used under the stricter terms), so asking for `policy="LEGACY"` returns every site,
while the default labels US-Ha1 `CCBY4.0` and CA-Let `LEGACY`.

For the sites you name, the result also lists:

- **`emptySites`**: requested sites without data for a product, and why (a Legacy site
  has no FLUXNET product; RU-Sam has no Tier One years; no data in your year window);
- **`policyVerdict`**: the policy the selection must follow per product, with its
  obligations: mixing CC-BY and Legacy sites means Legacy, mixing tiers means Tier Two;
- **`combinedObligations`**: every obligation once, across collections.

An impossible product and policy pair (FLUXNET under LEGACY, BASE-BADM under TIER2)
fails with `invalid_argument` before any request: the AmeriFlux API would answer it
with empty rows rather than an error.

## Resources

| URI | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `ameriflux://site/{site_id}` | One site's card (the `amf_get_site` result) |
| `ameriflux://reference/vocabularies` | IGBP classes and Köppen climates in AmeriFlux's wording, the product × policy matrix, intended-use codes, member networks |
| `ameriflux://reference/neon-crosswalk` | NEON site codes and their AmeriFlux sites, from the live catalog |
| `ameriflux://reference/lter-crosswalk` | AmeriFlux sites linked to LTER sites and EDI scopes (draft) |

# Local files

Three tools read the AmeriFlux and FLUXNET files already on your computer. They run only
over **stdio** (a hosted server has no access to your disk), never use the network, and
read archives **in place**: nothing is extracted. Inputs and result fields are in the
[Tool reference](reference.md).

## Where they look

Files are readable only inside the **download directory** (`downloads.directory`,
default `~/ameriflux-downloads`) and any folder in **`local.roots`**
([Configuration](../getting-started/configuration.md)):

```bash
export AMERIFLUX_MCP_LOCAL__ROOTS=~/fluxnet2015,~/flux-archive
```

Paths are relative to a root (or absolute inside one). `archive.zip::member.csv` names
a member. A path that leaves the roots, including through a symbolic link, fails with
`invalid_argument` (`outside_local_roots`). FLUXNET2015 zips need a fluxnet.org account,
so you download them yourself and add their folder to `local.roots`; the server never
automates that login.

## amf_list_files

Lists every file whose name AmeriFlux or FLUXNET gave it, and classifies each archive
member[^research]:

| Family | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `base` | `AMF_<SITE>_BASE-BADM_<X-Y>.zip` holding `AMF_<SITE>_BASE_(HH\|HR)_<X-Y>.csv` and the site's BIF workbook |
| `bif` | `AMF_<SITE>_BIF_<date>.xlsx`, and the bulk `AA-Flx`/`AA-Net` files |
| `fluxnet` | AmeriFlux FLUXNET (ONEFlux v1.3) zips: FLUXMET, ERA5 and BIFVARINFO files per resolution, a BIF CSV, README and licence[^oneflux-readme] |
| `fluxnet2015` | FULLSET and SUBSET zips: data per resolution, ERAI, AUXMETEO and AUXNEE |
| `fluxnet_ch4` | Listed; reading arrives in v0.2 |

Each entry gives the site, resolution, years and version; members that cannot be read
say why (see [Safety](#safety)). Filter by `family` or `site`, or give a folder or a
single archive as `path`.

## amf_preview_data

Reads one CSV, by `file` or by `site` and `product` (the newest local version), and by
default the half-hourly or hourly member of an archive (`resolution` picks another).

- **Summary** (default): per column the count, missing values (`-9999`), min, max, mean,
  units at the file's resolution, and `outOfRange`: values beyond the FP Standard range
  ±5%, counted but kept. The file info gives the time step read from the timestamps,
  the time range, the `#` header lines of BASE files, and the site's UTC offsets.
- **Rows** (`mode='rows'`): a page of rows (`max_rows`, `offset`) within `start`/`end`.
  `to_utc=true` adds UTC timestamps, applying the offset in force on each row's date.
- **QC**: `qc_max` keeps HH/HR values whose `_QC` flag is at most the threshold (0
  measured … 3 poor); `qc_min_fraction` keeps DD and coarser values whose QC fraction
  is at least the threshold. Rejected values become null and are counted in
  `qcFiltered`.
- **SUBSET view**: `view='subset'` keeps only the FLUXNET2015 SUBSET variables of an
  AmeriFlux FLUXNET file.
- **Aux tables**: AUXMETEO and AUXNEE are read as plain tables, with text values
  listed.

```json
{"tool": "amf_preview_data", "arguments": {"site": "US-Ha1", "product": "FLUXNET", "resolution": "DD", "columns": ["NEE_VUT_REF", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF"], "qc_min_fraction": 0.8}}
{"tool": "amf_preview_data", "arguments": {"file": "AMF_US-Ha1_BASE-BADM_28-5.zip", "mode": "rows", "start": "2020-07-01", "end": "2020-07-02", "to_utc": true}}
```

!!! note "HH can mean hourly"

    ONEFlux v1.3 names its finest resolution `HH` even for hourly sites; the preview
    reads the step from `TIMESTAMP_START`/`TIMESTAMP_END` and says so when they differ.

A scan stops after `end`, or once it has read 256 MiB or run for 20 s
(`truncatedReason: budget`). Half-hourly BASE files reach hundreds of megabytes, so for
long records start with the DD or MM file, or narrow `start`, `end` and `columns`.

## amf_read_bif

Reads BADM Interchange Format files: the BIF workbook of a BASE-BADM zip, the BIF CSV of
a FLUXNET zip, or a BIF file on its own. It returns entries by group (filter with
`groups`, and with `site_id` in bulk files), the UTC offsets with their start dates, the
DOI and citation recorded for that version, and the funding acknowledgments.

**Personal data is withheld by default**: emails, postal and shipping addresses, and the
names of private land owners. They are shown only when you pass `include_contacts` and
the operator enabled `privacy.allow_contact_emails`. The citation in a BIF is the one of
that file's version; `amf_get_citation` gives the current one.

## Safety

Archives are read in place through a checker that refuses members with absolute or
`..` paths, symbolic links, encrypted members, members over 1 GiB uncompressed, and
members over 1 MiB that compress more than 200:1 (zip bombs)[^design]. Reads also stop if
a member decompresses past its declared size.

## Resources

| URI | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `ameriflux://guide/file-formats` | File names, CSV conventions, BIF and previews, for agents |
| `ameriflux://guide/fluxnet2015-access` | Getting FLUXNET2015 zips yourself and reading them here |

[^design]: ameriflux-mcp design. <https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp/blob/main/DESIGN.md>
[^oneflux-readme]: ONEFlux FLUXNET data product README. <https://github.com/fluxnet/ONEFlux/blob/main/oneflux/metadata/fluxnet_data_docs/README.txt>

# Tool reference

Generated from the tool registry by `scripts/gen_tools_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. 11 tools are registered; `amf_list_files`, `amf_preview_data`, `amf_read_bif` are offered only over stdio. Inputs are snake_case and outputs camelCase. Every result also carries `resolved`, `notes`, `nextSteps` and `source` (whose `backend` says what answered: the AmeriFlux API, its file server, or nothing upstream), and failures return `structuredContent.error` with a stable `code`. Tools still to come are on the [roadmap](roadmap.md).

## amf_describe_variables

**Describe variable names: grammar, units, QC and sites.** Decode up to 20 variable names from BASE or FLUXNET files: base name and FP Standard definition with QA/QC range, qualifiers (_PI, _QC, _F, _IU), position (_H_V_R, _H_V_A, _#), FLUXNET processing tokens (MDS, VUT/CUT, NT/DT, REF, percentiles), units and QC meaning per resolution, sign conventions. With site: whether the site measures it, sensor heights and instruments, yearly coverage. Next: call amf_get_availability for the site's years.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `variables` |
| Download identity | not needed |
| Transports | http, stdio |
| Annotations | readOnly=true, destructive=false, idempotent=true, openWorld=true |
| Upstream endpoints | `GET amfcdn.lbl.gov/api/v1/fp_var` |

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `names` | array of string | yes |  | Variable names as in file headers: TA_F_1_1_1, FC_PI_F_1_1_A, GPP_NT_VUT_REF, NEE_VUT_05, TS_F_MDS_2_QC … (min items 1; max items 20) |
| `resolution` | string \\| null |  | null | HH (also HR), DD, WW, MM or YY: units and QC meaning at this resolution (FLUXNET). Default: all resolutions. |
| `site` | string \\| null |  | null | A site (ID, NEON code or name): adds whether it measures the variable, its measurement heights and instruments, and yearly coverage. (max length 200) |

**Result fields** (besides the common envelope)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variables` | array of VariableDescription |  |
| `page` | Page |  |

## amf_get_availability

**Get data availability per site and product.** Published years per site for AmeriFlux BASE-BADM and FLUXNET (FLUXNET-1F), FLUXNET2015 and FLUXNET-CH4, and BADM (BIF) membership, each labelled with the data policy it is shared under (CC-BY-4.0, Legacy, Tier Two). Lists requested sites without data and why, and the policy the selection must follow with its obligations. Invalid product/policy pairs fail before any request. Next: call amf_get_citation for these sites.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `availability` |
| Download identity | not needed |
| Transports | http, stdio |
| Annotations | readOnly=true, destructive=false, idempotent=true, openWorld=true |
| Upstream endpoints | `GET amfcdn.lbl.gov/api/v1/data_availability/{network}/{product}/{policy}`<br>`GET amfcdn.lbl.gov/api/v1/site_availability`<br>`GET amfcdn.lbl.gov/api/v2/site_info_display/AmeriFlux` |

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sites` | array of string \\| null |  | null | Site IDs, NEON codes or names (up to 50). Omit for every site with data. (max items 50) |
| `products` | array of string \\| null |  | null | BASE-BADM, BIF, FLUXNET, FLUXNET2015, FLUXNET-CH4. Default: the products of each site's collections (BASE-BADM and FLUXNET for AmeriFlux sites), or BASE-BADM when no sites are given. (max items 5) |
| `policy` | string \\| null |  | null | CCBY4.0, LEGACY or TIER2: only data usable under that policy. Default: every row labelled with its own policy. |
| `years` | string \\| null |  | null | Only years in this window: '2015' or '2010-2015'. |
| `limit` | integer |  | `50` | >= 1; <= 200 |
| `offset` | integer |  | `0` | >= 0 |

**Result fields** (besides the common envelope)

| `summary` | AvailabilitySummary |  |
| `page` | Page |  |

**Get a site's BADM metadata.** A site's Biological, Ancillary, Disturbance and Metadata as the API exposes it, by group: location, IGBP and climate, tower dates, team (no emails by default), disturbance and management, funding sponsors and organizations (needed to acknowledge Legacy sites), reference papers, and instruments with measurement heights. The full BADM ships as the BIF file in BASE-BADM downloads. Next: call amf_get_citation to cite the site.

## amf_get_citation

**Get citations and acknowledgments for sites.** Citations for up to 50 sites and one product (BASE-BADM, BIF, FLUXNET, FLUXNET2015): AmeriFlux's own versioned text per site DOI (e.g. 'Ver. 28-5'), the policy the selection must follow with its obligations (mixing CC-BY and Legacy means Legacy; mixing tiers means Tier Two), verbatim acknowledgments, Legacy site funding, the data-availability sentence and processing papers. Optional BibTeX. Next: cite every site in the reference list and follow the obligations.

## amf_ping

**Check ameriflux-mcp status.** Liveness and capability report: server version, protocol and transport; whether a download identity is configured (booleans and profile names only, never the values) and which tools need it; whether downloads are enabled and where files go. With check_api=true it also makes one small request to the AmeriFlux API to confirm connectivity. Next: read ameriflux://guide/identity to set up downloads.

## amf_preview_data

**Preview a local AmeriFlux or FLUXNET data file.** Summarize or page through a local BASE, AmeriFlux FLUXNET or FLUXNET2015 CSV, in place or inside its zip: time step and range, per-column count, missing (-9999), min, max, mean and out-of-range counts, units per resolution, a time window, a QC filter, UTC timestamps from the site's BIF, a SUBSET column view, and aux tables. Stops within a byte and time budget. stdio only. Next: call amf_describe_variables on columns to decode.

## amf_search_sites

**Search AmeriFlux and FLUXNET sites.** Find flux tower sites in the AmeriFlux (856), FLUXNET2015 (212) and FLUXNET-CH4 (81) catalogs by words, place (bbox or near a point), IGBP ecosystem, Köppen climate, country/state, status, member network (NEON, LTER, ...), data product and policy, years with data, measured variables or gas species. Returns compact site summaries with years per product, facets over all matches, and paging. Next: call amf_get_site for one site or amf_get_availability for exact years.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `discovery` |
| Download identity | not needed |
| Transports | http, stdio |
| Annotations | readOnly=true, destructive=false, idempotent=true, openWorld=true |
| Upstream endpoints | `GET amfcdn.lbl.gov/api/v2/site_info_display/AmeriFlux`<br>`GET amfcdn.lbl.gov/api/v1/site_display/FLUXNET/FLUXNET2015`<br>`GET amfcdn.lbl.gov/api/v1/site_display/FLUXNET/FLUXNET-CH4` |

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string \\| null |  | null | Words matched against site ID, name, state, country, NEON code and networks (every word must match; prefixes count, e.g. 'harv'). (max length 200) |
| `collection` | `ameriflux` \\| `fluxnet2015` \\| `fluxnet_ch4` \\| `all` |  | `"all"` | ameriflux (856 sites), fluxnet2015 (212), fluxnet_ch4 (81) or all. |
| `product` | string \\| null |  | null | Only sites with data in BASE-BADM, FLUXNET (FLUXNET-1F), FLUXNET2015 or FLUXNET-CH4. |
| `policy` | string \\| null |  | null | CCBY4.0, LEGACY (AmeriFlux) or TIER2 (Tier-Two-only FLUXNET2015/CH4 sites). CC-BY-4.0, Legacy and Tier2 spellings are accepted. |
| `igbp` | array of string \\| null |  | null | IGBP classes, e.g. ['DBF', 'ENF'] (see the vocabulary). (max items 17) |
| `koeppen` | array of string \\| null |  | null | Köppen codes or prefixes, e.g. ['Dfb'] or ['B']. (max items 30) |
| `country` | array of string \\| null |  | null | Country codes as in site IDs ('US', 'CA', 'BR') or names ('Canada'). (max items 50) |
| `state` | array of string \\| null |  | null | US state or province codes, e.g. ['NM', 'AZ']. (max items 60) |
| `status` | `active` \\| `inactive` \\| `any` |  | `"any"` | AmeriFlux tower status. |
| `network` | array of string \\| null |  | null | Member networks besides AmeriFlux, e.g. ['NEON'], ['LTER'], ['Phenocam']. (max items 12) |
| `bbox` | array of number \\| null |  | null | [west, south, east, north] in decimal degrees (no antimeridian crossing). (min items 4; max items 4) |
| `near` | Near \\| null |  | null | Sites within radius_km of a point. |
| `years` | string \\| null |  | null | Data overlapping a year or range ('2015', '2010-2015') in the chosen product (default: BASE for AmeriFlux sites, the FLUXNET tier range otherwise). |
| `min_years` | integer \\| null |  | null | At least this many data years. (>= 1; <= 100) |
| `base_variable` | array of string \\| null |  | null | FP Standard base names every site must measure, e.g. ['FCH4', 'SWC']. (max items 20) |
| `gas` | array of string \\| null |  | null | Flux gas species, e.g. ['CH4'] or ['CO2', 'H2O']. (max items 6) |
| `sort` | `site_id` \\| `name` \\| `years` \\| `distance` \\| null |  | null | Default: distance with near, relevance with query, else site_id. |
| `limit` | integer |  | `25` | >= 1; <= 200 |
| `offset` | integer |  | `0` | >= 0 |

**Result fields** (besides the common envelope)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sites` | array of SiteSummary |  |
| `facets` | Facets | Counts over every match, not just this page. |
| `page` | Page |  |

## amf_search_variables

**Search the FP Standard and FLUXNET variable dictionaries.** Find variable names in the FP Standard list (AmeriFlux BASE, live, with QA/QC ranges) and the FLUXNET dictionaries (AmeriFlux FLUXNET from ONEFlux v1.3; FLUXNET2015 FULLSET and SUBSET), by words, category or resolution. FLUXNET units change with resolution (NEE is umol m-2 s-1 at HH, gC m-2 d-1 at DD), so each result lists units per resolution and SUBSET membership. Next: call amf_describe_variables on the names.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `variables` |
| Download identity | not needed |
| Transports | http, stdio |
| Annotations | readOnly=true, destructive=false, idempotent=true, openWorld=true |
| Upstream endpoints | `GET amfcdn.lbl.gov/api/v1/fp_var` |

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string \\| null |  | null | Words matched against name, description and units (prefixes count: 'soil temp', 'GPP', 'methane'). (max length 200) |
| `dictionary` | `fp` \\| `fluxnet` \\| `fluxnet_fullset` \\| `fluxnet_subset` \\| `all` |  | `"all"` | fp (FP Standard, BASE), fluxnet (AmeriFlux FLUXNET, ONEFlux v1.3), fluxnet_fullset / fluxnet_subset (FLUXNET2015), or all. |
| `category` | string \\| null |  | null | FP type (GASES, MET_RAD, MET_SOIL, …) or FLUXNET section (PARTITIONING, NET ECOSYSTEM EXCHANGE, …); prefixes count. (max length 60) |
| `resolution` | string \\| null |  | null | HH (also HR), DD, WW, MM or YY: FLUXNET variables available at it, with its units. |
| `limit` | integer |  | `25` | >= 1; <= 200 |
| `offset` | integer |  | `0` | >= 0 |

**Result fields** (besides the common envelope)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variables` | array of VariableSummary |  |
| `facets` | VariableFacets |  |
| `page` | Page |  |
