# Roadmap

ameriflux-mcp is built in eight steps, one pull request each[^design]. This page lists
what each step delivers. Once tools exist, a generated tool reference replaces the
descriptions here.

## Build steps

| Step | Delivers | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Design, verified API research, a read-only API probe | done |
| 2 | The MCP core ported from edi-mcp, configuration, identity settings, `amf_ping`, CI | done |
| 3 | AmeriFlux API client, rate limiting, cache, site catalog and name resolution, policy engine, recorded test fixtures | done |
| 4 | Site discovery and availability tools | done |
| 5 | Variable, citation and BADM tools | done |
| 6 | Local file readers and previews | done |
| 7 | The download tool (merged only after AmeriFlux confirms third-party use) | next |
| 8 | Prompts, resources, full documentation, Docker image, PyPI release v0.1.0 | planned |

The [tool reference](reference.md) is generated from the server's registry and lists
exactly the tools the current build offers.

## Planned tools

| Tool | Step | HTTP | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amf_ping` | 2 | yes | Version, protocol, transport; which identity fields are configured (booleans only); whether the AmeriFlux API answers. |
| `amf_search_sites` | 4 | yes | Find AmeriFlux (856 sites), FLUXNET2015 (212) and FLUXNET-CH4 (81) towers[^research] by name, place, bounding box, IGBP ecosystem class, Köppen climate, years, product, data policy and measured variables. |
| `amf_get_site` | 4 | yes | One site by ID, name, NEON code or FLUXNET2015 alias: location, ecosystem, climate, data policy, DOIs, years per product, team (no emails by default) and links to NEON and EDI. |
| `amf_get_availability` | 4 | yes | Published years per site, product and policy, with the sites that have no data listed separately and the effective policy of the selection. |
| `amf_search_variables` | 5 | yes | Search the FP Standard (145 base names) and FLUXNET FULLSET/SUBSET dictionaries, with units per time resolution. |
| `amf_describe_variables` | 5 | yes | Parse names such as `TA_F_1_1_1` or `GPP_NT_VUT_REF`: qualifiers, gap-filling and partitioning method, QC scheme, units by resolution, sign convention, measurement heights. |
| `amf_get_citation` | 5 | yes | The versioned citation AmeriFlux recommends per site, required acknowledgments, the obligations of the CC-BY-4.0, Legacy or Tier 2 policy, and a data-availability sentence. |
| `amf_get_badm` | 5 | yes | Site metadata (BADM) the API exposes: location, IGBP, climate, team, disturbance and management, funding, reference papers, instruments and measurement heights. |
| `amf_download_data` | 7 | no | BASE-BADM, AmeriFlux FLUXNET and bulk BADM through AmeriFlux's logged download route: a plan first, then `confirm=true`; checksummed files. Needs a [download identity](../getting-started/identity.md). |
| `amf_list_files` | 6 | no | Classify downloaded zips and CSVs by product, site, resolution, years and version. |
| `amf_preview_data` | 6 | no | Column summaries and row windows from local BASE, FLUXNET and FLUXNET2015 files, with time windows, QC filtering, missing values as nulls and a SUBSET view. |
| `amf_read_bif` | 6 | no | Read BADM Interchange Format files (xlsx or CSV), including UTC offsets and the site's DOI citation. |

## Data products covered

| Product | Discover | Availability | Cite | Download | Read locally |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AmeriFlux BASE (BASE-BADM) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| AmeriFlux BADM / BIF | yes | yes (membership) | yes (BASE DOI) | yes (bulk) | yes |
| AmeriFlux FLUXNET (FLUXNET-1F) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| FLUXNET2015 FULLSET / SUBSET | yes | yes | yes | no (login-protected form) | yes |
| FLUXNET-CH4 | yes | yes | v0.2 | no | v0.2 |

## After v0.1.0

Version 0.2 focuses on analysis: server-side summaries by year, month or hour with QC
handling, Parquet export with a hand-off to the CyVerse Data Store and mesa-ducklake,
DuckDB as an optional extra, FLUXNET-CH4 readers and citations, and possibly the
European and Australian networks served through the FLUXNET Shuttle.

# Variables

Flux files name every column with a code such as `TA_F_1_1_1` or `GPP_NT_VUT_REF`. Two
tools turn those codes into something you can use. Neither needs an account, and both
work over stdio and HTTP. Inputs and result fields are in the
[Tool reference](reference.md).

## Two kinds of name

**BASE names** (AmeriFlux BASE, the FP Standard[^amf-variables]) are a base name and
qualifiers:

```
<BASE NAME>[_PI][_QC][_F][_IU][_H_V_R | _H_V_A | _#][_SD | _N]
```

| Part | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Base name | One of about 145 FP Standard names (`TA`, `FC`, `SW_IN`, `FETCH_70`, `FC_SSITC_TEST`) |
| `_PI` | Filtered or gap-filled by the tower team, independently of the network |
| `_QC` | Quality flag from AmeriFlux's central QA/QC |
| `_F` | Gap-filled |
| `_IU` | Instrument units (counts, mV) rather than standard units |
| `_H_V_R` | One sensor: horizontal position, vertical position (1 = highest or shallowest), replicate |
| `_H_V_A` | Replicates at one position, averaged |
| `_#` | Layer aggregate across horizontal positions |
| `_SD`, `_N` | Standard deviation and number of sensors in an aggregate |

**FLUXNET names** (FLUXNET2015 FULLSET and SUBSET[^fullset], and the AmeriFlux FLUXNET
product made with ONEFlux v1.3) add processing tokens: `_F_MDS` (gap-filled with MDS),
`_ERA` (downscaled from reanalysis), `_VUT`/`_CUT` (USTAR threshold varies by year or is
constant), `_REF` and the percentiles `_05` … `_95`, `_NT`/`_DT`/`_SR` (partitioning
method), `_RANDUNC`, `_CORR`, `_DAY`/`_NIGHT`, `_QC`.

## Units and QC change with resolution

FLUXNET files come at HH (half-hourly or hourly), DD, WW, MM and YY, and one name means
different units at each[^research]:

| Variable | HH | DD, WW, MM | YY |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NEE_VUT_REF`, `GPP_NT_VUT_REF`, `RECO_NT_VUT_REF` | µmolCO2 m-2 s-1 | gC m-2 d-1 | gC m-2 y-1 |
| `P_F` | mm (per interval) | mm d-1 | mm y-1 |
| `TA_F_MDS_QC` | 0 measured, 1 good, 2 medium, 3 poor gap-fill | fraction of measured and good data | fraction |

Every FLUXNET result carries `unitsByResolution`; pass `resolution` to get one unit and
the QC meaning at that resolution. Negative NEE and FC are uptake; GPP and RECO are
positive.

## amf_search_variables

Words match names, descriptions and units (prefixes count). Choose a `dictionary`:

| `dictionary` | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `fp` | The FP Standard list for BASE, read live from the AmeriFlux API with its QA/QC ranges (`plausibleRange`) |
| `fluxnet` | Names the AmeriFlux FLUXNET product defines (ONEFlux v1.3) |
| `fluxnet_fullset`, `fluxnet_subset` | FLUXNET2015 FULLSET (232 names) and SUBSET (72) |
| `all` | All of the above (default) |

`category` filters by FP type (`GASES`, `MET_SOIL`) or FLUXNET section (`PARTITIONING`,
`SUNDOWN`); `resolution` keeps the FLUXNET names produced at it.

```json
{"tool": "amf_search_variables", "arguments": {"query": "soil temperature"}}
{"tool": "amf_search_variables", "arguments": {"query": "GPP", "dictionary": "fluxnet_subset", "resolution": "DD"}}
```

Dictionary names with `XX` or `#` stand for many columns: `NEE_VUT_XX` is `NEE_VUT_05`
to `NEE_VUT_95`, and `TS_F_MDS_#` is `TS_F_MDS_1` (shallowest), `TS_F_MDS_2`, …

## amf_describe_variables

Up to 20 names per call. Each result gives the base name and its FP definition, every
qualifier or token with its meaning, the position, the units, the FLUXNET definition
(with the dictionary key: `NEE_VUT_05` is `NEE_VUT_XX`), a sign convention where one
applies, and `didYouMean` for names it does not recognize. A name valid in both grammars
(`TA_F`) gets both readings, with a note.

With `site`, each name also gets:

- whether the site's BASE data include the base name (from the catalog);
- sensor heights and instruments from AmeriFlux's measurement-height file;
- yearly coverage per column from amerifluxr's snapshot, marked with its date
  (2025-10-20 as of this writing; it lags the current BASE release).

```json
{"tool": "amf_describe_variables", "arguments": {"names": ["GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "TA_F_MDS_QC"], "resolution": "DD"}}
{"tool": "amf_describe_variables", "arguments": {"names": ["TA", "SWC_1_1_1"], "site": "US-Ha1"}}
```

The first call with `site` downloads the measurement-height file (about 2.3 MB) and the
coverage snapshot (about 6.5 MB). Both are cached: heights for 24 hours, coverage for
7 days.

## Sources and resources

| URI | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `ameriflux://guide/variable-grammar` | The grammar on this page, for agents |
| `ameriflux://reference/fp-variables` | The FP Standard list (live, or the bundled snapshot when the API is unreachable) |
| `ameriflux://reference/fluxnet-variables` | The FLUXNET dictionary with units and notes per resolution |

The FLUXNET dictionary is built by `scripts/build_variable_dictionaries.py` from the
FLUXNET2015 webdoc dictionaries and ONEFlux's `var_info_definitions` files. The micro
sign is restored where ONEFlux stores it as a replacement character[^design].

# For AI agents

This site is published for people **and** for AI agents. The documentation
source is an [Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md){target=_blank}
knowledge bundle[^okf-spec], and the deployed site exposes that structure
directly. If you are an agent (or you are wiring one up), consume the
documentation through the endpoints below rather than scraping rendered HTML.

## This site documents an MCP server

ameriflux-mcp *is* an agent tool. If what you actually want is AmeriFlux or
FLUXNET data — sites, availability, variables, citations — do not scrape these
pages: connect to the server and call its tools. Locally, run it over `stdio`
(`claude mcp add ameriflux -s user -- ameriflux-mcp --transport stdio`); against a
hosted instance, use Streamable HTTP at `https://<host>/mcp`
(`claude mcp add --transport http ameriflux https://<host>/mcp`). The server is
under construction; the [roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md) says which tools exist. The server
implements MCP 2026-07-28[^mcp-spec]: `server/discover` and `tools/list`
return the live, authoritative tool catalogue with JSON Schema inputs and
outputs, and every list result carries cache hints. Use this documentation
to learn *how* to use the server; use the server to get the data.

## Entry points

All URLs are under `https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/`.

| Endpoint | What you get |
| -------- | ------------ |
| [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt) — `https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/llms.txt` | Linked outline of every page with one-line descriptions ([llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org){target=_blank}[^llmstxt]) |
| [`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt) — `https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/llms-full.txt` | The entire corpus in one file: every page's Markdown with frontmatter, each prefixed by its canonical URL |
| Any page URL + `index.md` | That page's Markdown source with full OKF frontmatter, e.g. `https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/getting-started/install/index.md` |
| `https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/sitemap.xml`, `https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/robots.txt` | Standard crawl surface; `robots.txt` welcomes AI fetchers and repeats these pointers |
| [`tools/reference/`](../tools/reference.md) — `https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/tools/reference/` | The tool catalogue generated from the server's registry: every tool's inputs, result fields, endpoints and identity requirement |
| [`tools/roadmap/`](../tools/roadmap.md) — `https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/tools/roadmap/` | The planned tools and the build step that delivers each |
| [Source repository](https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp){target=_blank} | The bundle itself under `docs/`, plus `CLAUDE.md` with the rules coding agents follow when editing the code |

Every rendered page also declares its Markdown twin and OKF signals in its
HTML `<head>`, as `okf:`-prefixed meta tags named after the frontmatter keys
(`type`, `status`, `trust-tier`, `generated-at`, `generated-by`,
`stale-after`) — for example:

```html
<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="index.md">
<meta name="okf:status" content="stable">
<meta name="okf:trust-tier" content="unverified">
<meta name="okf:generated-at" content="2026-10-23T00:00:00Z">
<meta name="okf:generated-by" content="claude/opus-5.5">
<meta name="okf:stale-after" content="2027-04-23T00:00:00Z">
```

The page's `type` is exposed the same way, so a crawler can filter by kind of
page (Guide, Reference, Policy, ...) without parsing frontmatter.

## Reading the OKF frontmatter

Each content page's YAML frontmatter answers the questions an agent should
ask before relying on it[^okf-spec]:

* **What is this?** — `type` (`Guide`, `Tutorial`, `Reference`, `Policy`,
  `MCP Tool Reference`), `title`, `description`, `tags`.
* **Where did it come from?** — `generated: { by, at }` records the actor
  that produced the current text and when it last changed meaningfully;
  `sources` lists the load-bearing external references (`id`, `resource`
  URL, `title`, `author`). Footnotes in the body cite sources by their `id`.
* **How much should I trust it?** — the `verified` key (see trust tiers
  below). Its absence is meaningful: the page has not been confirmed by
  anyone other than its generator.
* **Is it still true?** — `status` (`stable` is the default; `draft` needs
  review; `deprecated` is kept for history only) and `stale_after`, an
  ISO 8601 instant after which the page should be re-checked. Pages that
  state facts AmeriFlux, FLUXNET or the MCP project may change — data
  policies, endpoints, SDK versions — carry one.

Actors follow OKF §7: `<producer>/<version>` for agents and tools (for
example `claude/opus-5.5`), `human:<id>` for a person, `process:<id>` for an
automated job such as the generated tool reference.

## Trust tiers

| `verified` key | Tier | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| absent | **unverified** | Generated content nobody has confirmed against its sources. Most pages on this site start here. |
| present, non-`human:` actors only | **machine-confirmed** | An automated check (a CI job, a live smoke test) confirmed the content. |
| present with a `human:<id>` actor | **human-reviewed** | A maintainer read and confirmed the page. Prefer these when answers conflict. |

Only humans add `verified:` entries; a generator never does. The
`okf:trust-tier` meta tag carries the derived tier for quick filtering.

## Answering user questions

Ground answers in this documentation and cite the page URL (for example
`https://idss-mesa.github.io/ameriflux-mcp/getting-started/install/`). For
anything about the *data* — site IDs, years, variables, DOIs, policies — call
the server or [AmeriFlux](https://ameriflux.lbl.gov){target=_blank}
rather than guessing from prose. When the corpus does not answer a question
about ameriflux-mcp itself, direct users to the
[GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp/issues){target=_blank}.

[^okf-spec]: Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2 specification. <https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md>
[^llmstxt]: The /llms.txt convention. <https://llmstxt.org>
[^mcp-spec]: Model Context Protocol specification, 2026-07-28. <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28>

# Citing AmeriFlux and FLUXNET data

AmeriFlux and FLUXNET data come from individual tower teams, and the data policies ask
you to credit each site you use. `amf_get_citation` assembles everything on this page
for a list of sites; this page explains what it returns and why. The text below follows
the AmeriFlux data policy (CC-BY-4.0 license revised December 2025) and the FLUXNET data
policy as read on 2026-10-22[^amf-policy][^fluxnet-policy]; the policy pages are
authoritative.

## One citation per site

Every AmeriFlux product of every site has its own DOI under `10.17190/AMF/`, and every
FLUXNET2015 site one under `10.18140/FLX/`. Cite each site in the reference list, not in
supplementary material. AmeriFlux's recommended form includes the product version:

> J. William Munger, Shawn Urbanski, Michael Golden, Carol Barford, Jaclyn Matthes,
> Steven Wofsy (2026), AmeriFlux BASE US-Ha1 Harvard Forest EMS Tower (HFR1), Ver. 28-5,
> AmeriFlux AMP, (Dataset). https://doi.org/10.17190/AMF/1246059

> … (2026), AmeriFlux FLUXNET-1F US-Ha1 Harvard Forest EMS Tower (HFR1), Ver. v1.3_r1
> (1991-2025), AmeriFlux AMP, (Dataset). https://doi.org/10.17190/AMF/1871137

The version, year and publisher in this form differ from what generic DOI services
(DataCite, doi.org) return, so prefer AmeriFlux's form. BADM metadata downloaded with a
product is cited with that product's DOI. AmeriFlux does not publish ready-made citation
text for FLUXNET2015 sites; `amf_get_citation` builds it from the site's DOI record in the
form the FLUXNET DOI landing page shows:

> J. William Munger, Shawn Urbanski, Michael Golden, Carol Barford, Jaclyn Matthes,
> Steven Wofsy (1991-2012) FLUXNET2015 US-Ha1 Harvard Forest EMS Tower (HFR1), Dataset.
> https://doi.org/10.18140/FLX/1440071

## Acknowledgments

For **CC-BY-4.0** AmeriFlux data:

> Funding for the AmeriFlux data service was provided by the U.S. Department of Energy
> Office of Science.

For **Legacy** data the wording names the data *portal*:

> Funding for the AmeriFlux data portal was provided by the U.S. Department of Energy
> Office of Science.

When you use the **AmeriFlux FLUXNET** product, add:

> FLUXNET data products were produced and harmonized by eddy covariance regional
> networks and data processing centers, including AmeriFlux, ChinaFlux, European Fluxes
> Database, ICOS, JapanFlux, KoFlux, OzFlux, SAEON, and TERN. These products also include
> a modified version of ERA5 hourly data provided by the Copernicus Climate Change
> Service.

## Processing references

- AmeriFlux BASE: Chu, H., Christianson, D.S., Cheah, YW. et al. AmeriFlux BASE data
  pipeline to support network growth and data sharing. *Sci Data* 10, 614 (2023).
  https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-023-02531-2[^chu-2023]
- AmeriFlux FLUXNET and FLUXNET2015: Pastorello, G. et al. The FLUXNET2015 dataset and
  the ONEFlux processing pipeline for eddy covariance data. *Sci Data* 7, 225 (2020).
  https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3[^pastorello-2020]

## Data availability statement

If your paper has a data availability section, the AmeriFlux policy suggests:

> The AmeriFlux [DATA PRODUCT] were accessed from [SOURCE] on XX Month YYYY

where [SOURCE] can be the AmeriFlux data portal, AmeriFlux APIs, the FLUXNET User
Interface for the Shuttle, or the FLUXNET Shuttle code. Data downloaded through
ameriflux-mcp came through the AmeriFlux APIs.

## What each policy asks of you

| Policy | Obligations |
| --- | --- |
| AmeriFlux CC-BY-4.0 | Cite each site's DOI; include the DOE acknowledgment; add the data availability sentence when the paper has that section; informing data providers about publications is recommended. |
| AmeriFlux Legacy | Contact the site PIs when you start in-depth analysis (they may offer co-authorship); cite each DOI; acknowledge site funding; include the DOE "data portal" acknowledgment; inform providers before publication; use the AmeriFlux logo or link in presentations. |
| FLUXNET2015 Tier 1 | CC-BY-4.0: cite Pastorello et al. (2020); list each site by its FLUXNET ID and/or DOI; informing data providers is recommended. |
| FLUXNET2015 Tier 2 | Scientific and educational use; contact the data providers when you begin research that could lead to a publication; give them at least three weeks to contribute after the first draft; list each site in a table. Six sites are Tier 2 only (RU-Sam, RU-SkP, RU-Tks, RU-Vrk, SE-St1, ZA-Kru) and are not part of Pastorello et al. (2020). |

**Mixing escalates.** A study that combines CC-BY-4.0 and Legacy AmeriFlux data follows
the Legacy policy for all of it; one that combines FLUXNET2015 Tier 1 and Tier 2 data
treats all of it as Tier 2. `amf_get_citation` reports the effective policy for the
sites you name, with each obligation marked required or recommended, and
[Citations and BADM](../tools/citation.md) describes everything it returns.

## Citing ameriflux-mcp

ameriflux-mcp is software, not a data source: cite the data as above. If you want to
mention the tool, for example in a methods section:

> Data were discovered and retrieved with ameriflux-mcp (idss-mesa, University of New
> Mexico; https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp), version X.Y.Z.

[^amf-policy]: AmeriFlux Data Policy. <https://ameriflux.lbl.gov/data/data-policy/>
[^fluxnet-policy]: FLUXNET Data Policy. <https://fluxnet.org/data/data-policy/>
[^chu-2023]: Chu et al. (2023), Sci Data 10, 614. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-023-02531-2>
[^pastorello-2020]: Pastorello et al. (2020), Sci Data 7, 225. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3>

# License

Three things meet on this site: the server software, the documentation you are reading,
and the AmeriFlux and FLUXNET data the server gives access to. Each has its own terms.

## Server code — MIT

The ameriflux-mcp source code (the `ameriflux_mcp` Python package, the `ameriflux-mcp`
command-line program, tests and build scripts) is released under the
[MIT License](https://opensource.org/license/mit){target=_blank}[^mit]:

> Copyright (c) 2026 The Regents of the University of New Mexico

The full text is in the repository's
[`LICENSE`](https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE){target=_blank}
file[^ameriflux-mcp-license]. In short: you may use, copy, modify, merge, publish,
distribute, sublicense and sell the software, provided the copyright notice and
permission notice are included; the software is provided "as is", without warranty.
Code and data that ameriflux-mcp ports from other projects (amerifluxr, the FLUXNET
Shuttle, ONEFlux) keep their own BSD-style licenses and are credited in the repository's
[`NOTICE`](https://github.com/idss-mesa/ameriflux-mcp/blob/main/NOTICE){target=_blank}
file.

## Documentation text — CC-BY 4.0

The prose, tables and examples on this site (everything under `docs/` in the repository,
including the OKF frontmatter) are licensed under
[Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/){target=_blank}[^cc-by-4].
You may share and adapt the material for any purpose, provided you give appropriate
credit ("ameriflux-mcp documentation, idss-mesa / The Regents of the University of New
Mexico, CC-BY 4.0") and indicate whether changes were made. Code snippets embedded in the
documentation may alternatively be used under the MIT terms above. Quoted data-policy
text belongs to AmeriFlux and FLUXNET.

## Flux data — per site and product

Data retrieved through ameriflux-mcp are not part of this project and are not covered by
either license above. Each AmeriFlux site shares its data under the CC-BY-4.0 license or
the AmeriFlux Legacy policy, and FLUXNET2015 under Tier 1 (CC-BY-4.0) or Tier 2[^amf-policy].
Follow the policy of every site you use, and cite it as described in
[Citing AmeriFlux and FLUXNET data](citing-ameriflux.md).

## Trademarks and affiliation

ameriflux-mcp is an independent project of
[idss-mesa](https://github.com/idss-mesa){target=_blank} at the University of New
Mexico. It is not developed, endorsed or supported by the AmeriFlux Management Project,
Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, FLUXNET or the U.S. Department of Energy. Their
names belong to their respective owners; this site uses its own original artwork.
